title: Sagan–Carlotto correspondence on the Face on Mars
summary: Maaneli Derakhshani tells of Sagan–Carlotto correspondence on the Face on Mars, about 1980s at Cydonia, Mars, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: he even had correspondences with with Dr. Mark Carlott, one of the early researchers of the face on Mars, expressing interest in Carl's various analyses of the face on Mars.

plain: The Face on Mars is a hill in a region of Mars called Cydonia that looked like a human face in photos taken by a NASA probe. Maaneli Derakhshani, a researcher on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in the 1980s the astronomer Carl Sagan exchanged letters with Mark Carlotto, one of the first people to study the face, showing interest in his analyses, and he also names NASA scientist Gerald Soffen. If true, it would mean Sagan was more curious about the face than his public stance suggested.
